data.headline: Ten-year Treasury yield eases as thirty-year rises
data.summary: On November 24 the ten-year Treasury yield slipped one basis point to 4.91% while the thirty-year rose one to 5.30%. The two-year held at 4.63%.

bull.text: The ten-year yield fell from 4.92%. Its spread over the two-year narrowed from 29 to 28 basis points.

bear.text: The thirty-year yield moved up from 5.29%, leaving the longest benchmark with a higher borrowing rate than on November 23.

watch.text: The thirty-year yield finished 39 basis points above the ten-year, compared with 37 the previous session.

limitations: The Treasury series measures constant-maturity par yields. Equity ETF returns are measured separately.
